title: Lazur vs Aqua Voice on Mac: screen-aware dictation or a voice assistant
metaTitle: Lazur vs Aqua Voice: which one fits your Mac
description: Lazur vs Aqua Voice on Mac: both read your screen. Aqua uses it for dictation on every device; Lazur answers, points and guides. Prices from each site.
intro: Aqua Voice is AI dictation that uses your screen to type more accurately. Lazur uses your screen for more than typing: hold ⌥ ⌘ and it answers questions, points at buttons and walks you through apps.
tldr: Aqua Voice is a dictation tool. Lazur is a voice assistant that also dictates.
Pick Aqua Voice if typing by voice is all you need, on more devices.
Pick Lazur if you also want help with what is on your screen: answers, pointing at buttons, step-by-step guidance.
Lazur is free for 3 days, then $18/month.

faq.question: Is Lazur a good Aqua Voice alternative?
faq.answer: If you want more than dictation, yes. Lazur dictates in any Mac app and also answers questions about your screen, points at buttons and guides you. If you only dictate, Aqua Voice is a fine choice.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur and Aqua Voice together?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as their shortcuts do not clash. Lazur uses hold fn to dictate and hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask.

faq.question: Does Aqua Voice see my screen too?
faq.answer: Aqua lists screen awareness as a feature, used to improve dictation. Lazur uses the screen to answer questions and point at things.
